verdict.rationale: SES's own receipt rules let a user configure processing once, and SES then applies it automatically to every incoming email: storing it in S3, publishing to SNS, triggering Lambda, or sending bounce messages. Virtual Deliverability Manager can also automatically apply deliverability recommendations. These are event-triggered rules rather than a general automation or agent system, and anything beyond the built-in actions needs custom Lambda code the user writes. Missing for 10: a general-purpose automation or workflow builder, recurring or scheduled background jobs, autonomous multi-step logic without user-written code, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Receipt rules can do advanced processing such as deliver incoming mail to an Amazon S3 bucket, publish it to an Amazon SNS topic, send it to Amazon WorkMail, or automatically send bounce messages.
Take action on your received emails by triggering AWS Lambda functions.
Email senders can also enable Virtual Deliverability Manager to automatically implement recommendations that instantly improve their email deliverability.
